findings.reason: a §8 builder reads that the mode it must use is delivered by §6 and either waits on it or writes outside its own scope, and a §6 builder reading the plan's other half could add the same `runs.py` change in a file §6 does not own.
findings.text: §8's Why says "`_pointer_lock` … takes a blocking `flock(LOCK_EX)` only, so §6 gives it a non-blocking mode, and a resume takes the run's promotion lock first in that mode", but §6 now assigns that race away ("The race that let the pointer change … is §8") and its write paths drop `reckon/crew/runs.py` and `reckon/crew/resumption.py`, which §8's write paths carry — so the two sections name each other's work as the other's, and `plan-section-depends-on` records no `s8` entry either

response_events.note: §8 now gives _pointer_lock its non-blocking mode itself; §6 and §8 write disjoint files (§6: promotion.py, promotion_records.py, pending_landing.py; §8: runs.py, resumption.py), so §8 needs no wait

wiring-1.note: §8 now gives _pointer_lock its non-blocking mode itself; §6 and §8 write disjoint files (§6: promotion.py, promotion_records.py, pending_landing.py; §8: runs.py, resumption.py), so §8 needs no wait

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited anchor resolves in the tree as the plan describes it: `promotion.py:161` (`_promotion_lock`), `promotion.py:191` (the `changed while promotion ran` raise), `promotion.py:335-337` (the promotion's own lock order), `runs.py:453-462` (blocking `LOCK_EX` only), `resumption.py:217`, `promotion_checks.py:787`, `pending_landing.py:185/226-234`, `crew_run_commands.py:3217`, `recovery_review_acceptance.py:209-240/348`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each of §6, §7 and §8 states its measure with a declared negative control, and every control is a base-revision behaviour that was checked against the tree (`promotion.py`'s guard raising and preserving the pointer; `resumption.mark_resume_launching` taking the pointer lock unconditionally; `recovery_review_acceptance._commits_missing_from` probing local `HEAD`).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — all three sections put their logs and tests on paths that survive the run (the run directory, the repository's `tests/`), none in a scratchpad or node-local temp path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the added units name no tickets, plan labels or stage names; the `§N` references are prose cross-references inside the plan, not code identifiers.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — §6's cited cause matches its evidence (the guard at `promotion.py:191` raises before the merge, and `pending_landing.clear_pending` is reached only after a successful land, so the pending record §6 needs is still on disk when the guard raises); §8's lock argument is confirmed against the code (`_promotion_lock` is `_pointer_lock("promotion-<run>")`, a different lock file from the run's own pointer lock, so the measured concurrent mutation is explained, and the live-worker check sits inside the promotion lock at `promotion.py:589`, so the fixed order closes the window rather than narrowing it); §7's mechanism is reached from a real caller (`promotion_module.complete` at `recovery_review_acceptance.py:348`).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §6 carries only the pending-landing repair, §7 only the reflex-acceptance remote check, §8 only the resume-versus-promotion lock.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §8 attributes the non-blocking `_pointer_lock` to §6, while §6 now assigns it to §8 and §8's own write paths own it.
